questions.q: In the lesson's loan example, the group column was left out of the model, yet group B was approved far less often. Why?
options: Income and credit history acted as proxies that correlate with group
Logistic regression is biased by design
The test set contained only group A
Dropping a column always increases the selection gap
questions.explain: Removing a sensitive column does not remove the information it carries; correlated features such as income and history can act as proxies.

questions.q: What does the true positive rate (TPR) by group measure in the loan example?
options: The share of all applicants who were approved
The share of approved people who repaid
The share of people who would have repaid who were approved
The share of people who would not have repaid who were approved
questions.explain: TPR is approvals among those who would actually have repaid. The share of all applicants approved is the selection rate, and the share approved among those who would not repay is the FPR.

questions.q: When the lesson set a separate cutoff for group B to equalize selection rates, what happened?
options: TPR, FPR and precision also became equal
Only accuracy changed
TPR, FPR and precision stayed unequal between groups
The model stopped using income
questions.explain: Equal selection left TPR (0.784 vs 0.822), FPR and precision (0.668 vs 0.530) unequal, because the groups have different base rates.

questions.q: What is the best summary of how to choose among fairness definitions?
options: Pick whichever gives the highest accuracy and do not mention it
There is one universally correct definition that every model should satisfy
Fairness only matters if the sensitive column is a feature
It is a documented judgment about which errors matter most, made with legal, domain and affected-community input
questions.explain: Definitions conflict in general, so the choice is a transparent judgment, not a single number to optimize blindly.

questions.q: Which habit does the lesson call the key one when evaluating a model that affects people?
options: Slicing metrics by group and reporting sample sizes
Reporting only the overall accuracy
Removing all features that mention people
Using a 0.5 threshold for every group
questions.explain: One overall number hides who bears the errors; slice selection rate, TPR, FPR and precision by group, with sample sizes.
